tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

content.content:
### alloc accepts an empty shape as `ok` and creates nothing, which B5's `ok` effect does not allow; the choice is not documented
SUGG Report the empty shape (zero-element allocation) as a question for arbitration. Options: reject it as a static precondition, or accept `ok` with no root. Until then, state the current behaviour in the AllocStatic docstring and in the report (c).
REASON The facts hold, but this is not a formalization error. It is a gap in the sources that belongs in the pass-4 report.

Why the code is right:
- C6 fixes the encoding of `shape` as « au même encodage que les locaux de `enterFrame` (forêt indexée, parents d'indice inférieur) ». That encoding includes []: `EnterPre (write3Eff n6e [1]) [] []` decides true, and the module's own `rq1` enters a frame with empty locals.
- B5 says « `reject` pour toute précondition statique violée ». The static preconditions in B5 and C6 are the provider right, `Modify` on `owner`, and provider leaves `Init`. None of them requires a non-empty shape.
- Rejecting [] would need a precondition no source states. That breaks « rien d'inventé » and the rule that a definition is not stronger than its rule.
- The module documents how B5's single-root effect extends to forests. The `allocEff` docstring says « one root authority `Modify` per root element », and `alloc_owned_root` quantifies over `rootIdx`. Zero roots for [] follows directly.
- Any non-empty shape has a root, because element 0 has no parent under `ShapeOK`. So [] is the only case.
- No theorem holds only because of this case.

What survives: B5's `ok` effect, « nouvelle racine d'identité fraîche ... racine d'autorité `Modify` détenue par `owner` », cannot be produced for []. Neither B5 nor C6 addresses the zero-element case. For [] the result is `ok` and the state is unchanged: provider leaves are already `Init` by precondition, and `P` and `A` do not change. Under AGENTS.md (source silent or contradictory), this belongs in the report's open questions. The definition stays as it is.
EVID Checked in rev8/c6c9/judge1.lean, which exits 0:
- `AllocStep K0 1 0 [] (write3Eff n6e [1]) (.ok (allocEff (write3Eff n6e [1]) 1 0 [])) := .ok (by decide) trivial`
- `(allocEff ... []).P = (write3Eff n6e [1]).P ∧ (...).A = (...).A := by decide`
- `EnterPre (write3Eff n6e [1]) [] [] := by decide`

B5 (task_mm03_p3.md l.18): « `ok` : nouvelle racine d'identité fraîche, possédée par `owner`, feuilles `Uninit`, racine d'autorité `Modify` détenue par `owner` ». C6 (task_mm03_p4.md) on the shape encoding, quoted in the reasoning. `AllocStatic` (MM03.lean:3917) has no non-emptiness clause, and no source asks for one.

### Case 'arena whose storage comes from alloc' never checks that the alloc (and the write before it) is ok, or that ArenaInv holds
SUGG Add the three examples (Write3Step, AllocStep ... (.ok aa0), ArenaInv aa0 aar) next to the case.
REASON Confirmed for the alloc step:
- In `aa0`, the module builds the storage directly with `allocEff`, on `write3Eff (enter1 ...) [1]`.
- It checks only the two `IssueStep ... .ok` examples (MM03.lean:7413-7420).
- Nothing in the module shows that this `alloc` (or the provider write before it) is an accepted step. So the module never shows the case's premise, « le stockage vient de `alloc` » (task_mm03_p4.md, step 5).

(.ok (write3Eff (splitEff al2 2 [[3], [4]]) [3])) := .ok (by decide)
example : Write3Step 4 [4] (write3Eff (splitEff al2 2 [[3], [4]]) [3])
    (.ok (write3Eff (write3Eff (splitEff al2 2 [[3], [4]]) [3]) [4])) := .ok (by decide)

/-- An arena whose storage comes from `alloc`, two emissions (expected: `ok`, `ok`; C6). Frame 1:
0 arena value, 1 allocator value, 2 and 3 block destinations. The storage 4, with leaves 5 and 6,
is allocated and owned by 0; its root authority 4 is `internal`. The metadata right is
exercisable `Modify` on the arena value 0 (`MetaRight`, C6), without `SharedMutable`. -/
def aaE : S3 := enter1 [(none, none, 0), (none, none, 0), (none, none, 0), (none, none, 0)]
def aa0 : S3 := allocEff (write3Eff aaE [1]) 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0)]
example : Write3Step 1 [1] aaE (.ok (write3Eff aaE [1])) := .ok (by decide)
example : AllocStep K0 1 0 [(none, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0), (some 4, none, 0)]
    (write3Eff aaE [1]) (.ok aa0) := .ok (by decide) trivial
def aar : Arena := ⟨4, 4, [5, 6], []⟩
def aa1 : S3 × Arena := issueEff aa0 aar [5] 2
def aa2 : S3 × Arena := issueEff aa1.1 aa1.2 [6] 3
example : IssueStep K0 aar 0 [5] 2 aa0 (.ok aa1.1 aa1.2) := .ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
example : IssueStep K0 aa1.2 0 [6] 3 aa1.1 (.ok aa2.1 aa2.2) :=
  .ok (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)

/-- The same `alloc` twice, `Satisfiable` true then false depending on the state (expected: `ok`
then `fail`; C9). The allocator contract has a capacity of three places. -/
def KCap : K :=
  { KT [] [] [] [] [] with Satisfiable := fun _ ls s => s.P.length + ls.length ≤ 3 }
instance : DecidablePred KCap.SharedMutable :=
  fun l => inferInstanceAs (Decidable (l ∈ ([] : List Nat)))
instance : ∀ p ls s, Decidable (KCap.Satisfiable p ls s) := fun _ _ _ => Nat.decLe _ _
example : AllocStep KCap 1 0 [(none, none, 0)] (write3Eff n6e [1])
    (.ok (allocEff (write3Eff n6e [1]) 1 0 [(none, none, 0)])) := .ok (by decide) (by decide)
example : AllocStep KCap 1 0 [(none, none, 0)]
    (allocEff (write3Eff n6e [1]) 1 0 [(none, none, 0)])
    (.fail (allocEff (write3Eff n6e [1]) 1 0 [(none, none, 0)])) := .fail (by decide) (by decide)

/-- `alloc`, then a read of an `Uninit` leaf (expected: reject), a write (`ok`) and a read
(`ok`): the storage 2 of `n6a` before its write. -/
example : Read3Step 2 [2] (allocEff (write3Eff n6e [1]) 1 0 [(none, none, 0)]) .reject :=
  .reject (by decide)
example : Write3Step 2 [2] (allocEff (write3Eff n6e [1]) 1 0 [(none, none, 0)]) (.ok n6a) :=
  .ok (by decide)
example : Read3Step 2 [2] n6a (.ok n6a) := .ok (by decide)

/-- `transfer` of a local, source `Moved`, then a write into the source (`ok`) and a read
(`ok`): `mv1` above, where the value of local 1 went to 2. -/
example : Write3Step 1 [1] mv1 (.ok (write3Eff mv1 [1])) := .ok (by decide)
example : Read3Step 1 [1] (write3Eff mv1 [1]) (.ok (write3Eff mv1 [1])) := .ok (by decide)

/-- `transfer` of a part, the parent partly `Moved`, then a read of the other part (`ok`) and a
rewrite of the moved part (`ok`): in `c11a`, the part 1 of 0 goes to 3. -/
def tp1 : S3 := transferEff c11a 1 3
example : TransferStep K0 1 3 c11a (.ok tp1) := .ok (by decide)
example : tp1.I 1 = .moved ∧ tp1.I 2 = .init := by decide
example : Read3Step 0 [2] tp1 (.ok tp1) := .ok (by decide)
example : Write3Step 0 [1] tp1 (.ok (write3Eff tp1 [1])) := .ok (by decide)

/-- `endUse` of a local, then a write and a read in that local (expected: `ok`, `ok`; C8): the
local stays usable, its leaves `Uninit`. -/
example : EndUseStep K0 0 c13a (.ok (endUseEff c13a 0)) := .ok (by decide)
example : (endUseEff c13a 0).Usable 0 ∧ (endUseEff c13a 0).I 0 = .uninit := by decide
example : Write3Step 0 [0] (endUseEff c13a 0) (.ok (write3Eff (endUseEff c13a 0) [0])) :=
  .ok (by decide)
example : Read3Step 0 [0] (write3Eff (endUseEff c13a 0) [0])
    (.ok (write3Eff (endUseEff c13a 0) [0])) := .ok (by decide)

/-! ## Witnesses of the questions of pass 4 -/

/-- On every reached state, the base frame is 0, `nF` is positive, and no place is owned by frame
0: the initial state has one frame and no place (MM-03.3.1; pass-1 brief), `enterFrame` gives its
locals the new frame or a place as owner (A5), `alloc` and `transfer` only give places, and the
exit never pops the last frame (O7). -/
theorem reachable_base_owns_nothing {k : K} {s : S3} (h : Reachable k s) :
    s.F.getLast? = some 0 ∧ 0 < s.nF ∧ ∀ pl ∈ s.P, pl.owner ≠ .frame 0 := by
  induction h with
  | init => exact ⟨rfl, by decide, by simp [S3.init]⟩
  | derive _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | split _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | @release s s' a _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    unfold releaseEff; split <;> exact ih
  | @transfer s s' src dst _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    refine ⟨ih.1, ih.2.1, fun pl hpl => ?_⟩
    simp only [transferEff, List.mem_map] at hpl
    obtain ⟨pl₀, h₀, rfl⟩ := hpl
    split
    · simp
    · exact ih.2.2 pl₀ h₀
  | depend _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | @enter s s' ps ls _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    obtain ⟨h1, h2, h3⟩ := ih
    refine ⟨?_, by simp [enterEff], fun pl hpl => ?_⟩
    · show (s.nF :: s.F).getLast? = some 0
      cases hF : s.F with
      | nil => rw [hF] at h1; cases h1
      | cons a l => rw [hF] at h1; rw [List.getLast?_cons_cons]; exact h1
    · simp only [enterEff, enterP, List.mem_append, List.mem_map] at hpl
      rcases hpl with hpl | ⟨i, -, rfl⟩
      · exact h3 pl hpl
      · simp only [localOwner]; split
        · simp
        · intro e; injection e with e; omega
  | @exit s s' _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
    unfold exitEff
    unfold ExitPre at hpre
    split
    · rename_i f F₀ hF
      rw [hF] at hpre
      obtain ⟨hne, -⟩ := hpre
      refine ⟨?_, ih.2.1, ih.2.2⟩
      have := ih.1; rw [hF] at this
      cases F₀ with
      | nil => exact absurd rfl hne
      | cons g F₁ => rw [List.getLast?_cons_cons] at this; exact this
    · exact ih
  | read _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | write _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | writeShared _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | pin _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | unpin _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | endUse _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | free _ h ih =>
    obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; exact ih
  | @alloc s s' pr ow ls _ h ih =>
    cases h with
    | ok _ _ =>
      refine ⟨ih.1, ih.2.1, fun pl hpl => ?_⟩
      simp only [allocEff, allocP, shapeP, List.mem_append, List.mem_map] at hpl
      rcases hpl with hpl | ⟨i, -, rfl⟩
      · exact ih.2.2 pl hpl
      · simp only [shapeOwner]; split <;> simp

/-- On reached states, `StaticPinnedBottom` (C5) holds only for an empty static pinning: the base
frame, 0, owns no place (`reachable_base_owns_nothing`). `static_pinned_never_exits` then has no
content on reached states. -/
theorem staticPinnedBottom_forces_empty {k : K} {s : S3} (hr : Reachable k s)
    (hsp : StaticPinnedBottom k s) : ∀ l, ¬ k.Pinned l := by
  obtain ⟨hF, -, hP⟩ := reachable_base_owns_nothing hr
  intro l hl
  obtain ⟨q, -, hob⟩ := hsp l hl
  have hb : s.F.getLastD 0 = 0 := by
    rw [List.getLastD_eq_getLast?, hF]; rfl
  rw [hb] at hob
  induction hob with
  | frame hpl ho => exact hP _ (List.mem_of_getElem? hpl) ho
  | place _ _ _ ih => exact ih

/-- Reading the base frame of C5 as the first frame entered does not help: in `c13a`, the local 0
belongs to frame 1, the first frame entered, and stops being usable when frame 1 exits. -/
example : c13a.F = [1, 0] ∧ c13a.Usable 0 ∧ ¬ ({ c13a with F := [0] } : S3).Usable 0 ∧
    0 ∈ footprint c13a.P 0 ∧ OwnedByFrame c13a.P 1 0 :=
  ⟨rfl, by decide, by decide, by decide, .frame (pl := ⟨none, .frame 1, 0⟩) rfl rfl⟩

/-- `alloc` of the empty shape (C6): the encoding of the locals of `enterFrame` admits it, no
precondition excludes it, and the outcome is `ok` with no new place and no new authority, while
B5 describes `ok` as a new root. -/
example : AllocStep K0 1 0 [] (write3Eff n6e [1]) (.ok (allocEff (write3Eff n6e [1]) 1 0 [])) :=
  .ok (by decide) trivial
example : (allocEff (write3Eff n6e [1]) 1 0 []).P = (write3Eff n6e [1]).P ∧
    (allocEff (write3Eff n6e [1]) 1 0 []).A = (write3Eff n6e [1]).A := by decide

example : ReleaseStep 2 (deriveEff c13a 0 0 .observe)

/-- Reading the owned storage of a value shared in `Observe` (B2): the root of the storage, a
`Modify` authority held by the value, is exercisable at `Observe`, the mode the read requests
(pass 2: rejected). Writing it is rejected while the value is shared. Frame 1: 0 value, 2 owned
storage. -/
example : Read3Step 2 [2] n6a (.ok n6a) := .ok (by decide)
example : Read3Step 2 [2] (deriveEff n6a 0 0 .observe) (.ok (deriveEff n6a 0 0 .observe)) :=
  .ok (by decide)
example : Write3Step 2 [2] (deriveEff n6a 0 0 .observe) .reject := .reject (by decide)

/-- Witness state of `transfer_not_inv3_preserving`: place 1 is a part of place 0 with another
owner, a frame not on the stack; place 2 is owned by place 1 and anchored on 5, which does not
exist; place 3 is the destination. -/
def xferCex : S3 := ⟨[1, 0], 6, [⟨none, .frame 1, 0⟩, ⟨some 0, .frame 5, 0⟩, ⟨none, .place 1, 0⟩,
  ⟨none, .frame 1, 0⟩], fun l => if l = 1 then .init else .uninit,
  [⟨.modify, none, [1], .frame 1, true⟩, ⟨.modify, none, [3], .frame 1, true⟩],
  fun q => if q = 2 then [5] else [], fun _ => false, fun _ => false, fun _ => false⟩

/-- `transfer` (MM-03.3 §3, O4; A5) does not preserve `Inv3` alone (A1): a part with another
owner than its parent (excluded by `WF3`) is not usable while its parent is; a place owned by
that part is not usable either and keeps an invalid anchor. The transfer gives that place to the
destination: it becomes usable with an invalid anchor. -/
theorem transfer_not_inv3_preserving :
    Inv3 xferCex ∧ TransferStep K0 0 3 xferCex (.ok (transferEff xferCex 0 3)) ∧
      ¬ I3 (transferEff xferCex 0 3) := by
  refine ⟨⟨⟨fun a b x y p hab ha hb _ _ xp yp _ _ => ?_, fun b y a hb ho => ?_,
    fun q hq z hz => ?_, i4_always _⟩, fun q hq z hz => ?_⟩, .ok (by decide), fun h => ?_⟩
  · have h1 := lt_of_getElem? ha; have h2 := lt_of_getElem? hb
    simp [xferCex] at h1 h2
    obtain rfl | rfl : a = 0 ∨ a = 1 := by omega
    all_goals obtain rfl | rfl : b = 0 ∨ b = 1 := by omega
    all_goals first | exact absurd rfl hab |
      (simp [xferCex] at ha hb; subst ha hb; simp at xp yp; omega)
  · have := lt_of_getElem? hb; simp [xferCex] at this
    obtain rfl | rfl : b = 0 ∨ b = 1 := by omega
    all_goals simp [xferCex] at hb; subst hb; cases ho
  · cases Nat.decEq q 2 with
    | isTrue e => subst e; exact absurd hq (by decide)
    | isFalse e => simp [xferCex, e] at hz
  · cases Nat.decEq q 2 with
    | isTrue e => subst e; exact absurd hq (by decide)
    | isFalse e => simp [xferCex, e] at hz
  · exact absurd (h 2 (by decide) 5 (by decide)) (by decide)

/-- The witness of `transfer_not_inv3_preserving` breaks the parts clause of `WF3` and satisfies
all its other clauses, those of B1 and A4 included: the parts clause is the one needed. -/
example : (∀ (b : Nat) (y : Authority) (a : Nat), xferCex.A[b]? = some y → y.origin = some a →
      a < b) ∧
    (∀ (a : Nat) (x : Authority), xferCex.A[a]? = some x → ∀ l ∈ x.footprint,
      l < xferCex.P.length) ∧
    xferCex.F ≠ [] ∧ xferCex.F.Nodup ∧ (∀ f ∈ xferCex.F, f < xferCex.nF) ∧
    (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (f : Nat), xferCex.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .frame f →
      f < xferCex.nF) ∧
    (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (o : Nat), xferCex.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o →
      o < xferCex.P.length) ∧
    (∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority), xferCex.A[a]? = some y → y.active = true →
      HolderLive xferCex y.holder) ∧
    RootsDisjoint xferCex.P ∧ RootChain xferCex ∧ RootHeld xferCex ∧
    ¬ (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (r : Nat), xferCex.P[q]? = some pl → pl.parent = some r →
      ∃ pr : Place, xferCex.P[r]? = some pr ∧ r < q ∧ pr.owner = pl.owner ∧
        xferCex.dead r = xferCex.dead q) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, ?_, ?_, ?_, rootsDisjoint_always _, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro b y a hb ho
    have := lt_of_getElem? hb; simp [xferCex] at this
    obtain rfl | rfl : b = 0 ∨ b = 1 := by omega
    all_goals simp [xferCex] at hb; subst hb; cases ho
  · intro a x ha l hl
    have := lt_of_getElem? ha; simp [xferCex] at this
    obtain rfl | rfl : a = 0 ∨ a = 1 := by omega
    all_goals simp [xferCex] at ha; subst ha; simp at hl; subst hl; decide
  · intro q pl f hq ho
    have := lt_of_getElem? hq; simp [xferCex] at this
    obtain rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl : q = 0 ∨ q = 1 ∨ q = 2 ∨ q = 3 := by omega
    all_goals (simp [xferCex] at hq; subst hq; cases ho; try decide)
  · intro q pl o hq ho
    have := lt_of_getElem? hq; simp [xferCex] at this
    obtain rfl | rfl | rfl | rfl : q = 0 ∨ q = 1 ∨ q = 2 ∨ q = 3 := by omega
    all_goals (simp [xferCex] at hq; subst hq; cases ho; try decide)
  · intro a y ha hy
    have := lt_of_getElem? ha; simp [xferCex] at this
    obtain rfl | rfl : a = 0 ∨ a = 1 := by omega
    all_goals simp [xferCex] at ha; subst ha; decide
  · intro a y l ha hl _
    have := lt_of_getElem? ha; simp [xferCex] at this
    obtain rfl | rfl : a = 0 ∨ a = 1 := by omega
    · simp [xferCex] at ha; subst ha; simp at hl; subst hl
      exact ⟨0, _, 0, .inl rfl, rfl, rfl, by decide, by decide, fun l' => by
        rw [show footprint xferCex.P 0 = [1] by decide]⟩
    · simp [xferCex] at ha; subst ha; simp at hl; subst hl
      exact ⟨1, _, 3, .inl rfl, rfl, rfl, by decide, by decide, fun l' => by
        rw [show footprint xferCex.P 3 = [3] by decide]⟩
  · intro x z l r hx _ hl hr hlr
    have := lt_of_getElem? hx; simp [xferCex] at this
    obtain rfl | rfl : x = 0 ∨ x = 1 := by omega
    · simp [xferCex] at hx; subst hx; simp at hl; subst hl
      obtain rfl := rootOf_unique hr (show RootPlace xferCex.P 0 by decide) hlr (by decide)
      exact ⟨_, rfl, rfl⟩
    · simp [xferCex] at hx; subst hx; simp at hl; subst hl

  · cases Nat.decEq q 2 with
    | isTrue e => subst e; exact absurd hq (by decide)
    | isFalse e => simp [xferCex, e] at hz
  · cases Nat.decEq q 2 with
    | isTrue e => subst e; exact absurd hq (by decide)
    | isFalse e => simp [xferCex, e] at hz

/-- The witness of `transfer_not_inv3_preserving` breaks the parts clause of `WF3` and satisfies
all its other clauses, those of B1 and A4 included: the parts clause is the one needed. -/
example : (∀ (b : Nat) (y : Authority) (a : Nat), xferCex.A[b]? = some y → y.origin = some a →
      a < b) ∧
    (∀ (a : Nat) (x : Authority), xferCex.A[a]? = some x → ∀ l ∈ x.footprint,
      l < xferCex.P.length) ∧
    xferCex.F ≠ [] ∧ xferCex.F.Nodup ∧ (∀ f ∈ xferCex.F, f < xferCex.nF) ∧

/-- The witness of `transfer_not_inv3_preserving` in passes 2 and 3: place 1 is a part of place 0

def xferNd : S3 := ⟨[1, 0], 6, [⟨none, .frame 1, 0⟩, ⟨some 0, .frame 5, 0⟩, ⟨none, .place 1, 0⟩,
  ⟨none, .frame 1, 0⟩], fun l => if l = 1 then .init else .uninit,
  [⟨.modify, none, [1], .frame 1, true⟩, ⟨.modify, none, [3], .frame 1, true⟩,
    ⟨.modify, none, [], .frame 1, false⟩],
  fun q => if q = 2 then [2] else [], fun _ => false, fun _ => false, fun _ => false⟩

    (Inv3base xferNd ∧ AnchorOrder xferNd) ∧ ¬ NoDangling xferNd ∧

    obtain rfl | rfl | rfl : a = 0 ∨ a = 1 ∨ a = 2 := by omega

    all_goals first | exact absurd rfl hab |
      (simp [xferNd] at ha hb; subst ha hb; simp at xp yp <;> omega)
  · have := lt_of_getElem? hb; simp [xferNd] at this
    obtain rfl | rfl | rfl : b = 0 ∨ b = 1 ∨ b = 2 := by omega
    all_goals simp [xferNd] at hb; subst hb; cases ho
  · cases Nat.decEq q 2 with
    | isTrue e => subst e; exact absurd hq (by decide)
    | isFalse e => simp [xferNd, e] at hz

    | isFalse e => simp [xferNd, e] at hz

theorem allows_effOf {m m' : Mode} {ds : List Mode} (h : Allows (effOf m ds) m') :
    (ds = [] ∧ m'.le m) ∨ (Mode.modify ∉ ds ∧ m' = .observe) := by
  unfold Allows OptP at h
  split at h
  · rename_i e he
    rcases effOf_cases he with ⟨h0, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, hn, rfl⟩
    · exact .inl ⟨h0, h⟩
    · exact .inr ⟨hn, Mode.le_observe h⟩
  · exact h.elim

/-! ## Invariants (MM-03.3 §2, A1) -/

/-- I1, effective exclusivity strengthened structurally (MM-03.3 §2, A1): two distinct active
authorities, unrelated by `origin`, covering the same leaf, `SharedMutable` leaves included,
both have the proper mode `Observe`. The pass-1 statement on effective modes is the theorem
`effective_compat`. -/
def I1 (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (a b : Nat) (x y : Authority) (p : Nat), a ≠ b → s.A[a]? = some x → s.A[b]? = some y →
    x.active = true → y.active = true → p ∈ x.footprint → p ∈ y.footprint →
    a ∉ s.ancs b → b ∉ s.ancs a → x.mode = .observe ∧ y.mode = .observe

/-- I2, conservation of authorities (MM-03.3 §2): the origin of a derived authority exists, and
on each leaf of the derived footprint, the leaf is in the footprint of the origin and the
derived mode does not exceed the origin's. -/
def I2 (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (b : Nat) (y : Authority) (a : Nat), s.A[b]? = some y → y.origin = some a →
    ∃ x : Authority, s.A[a]? = some x ∧ ∀ p ∈ y.footprint, p ∈ x.footprint ∧ y.mode.le x.mode

/-- I3, validity of dependencies (MM-03.3 §2): every anchor of a usable place is valid, that is,
active (pass-1 arbitrage 2). -/
def I3 (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, s.Active x

/-- I4, validity of consumed values (MM-03.3 §2), first sentence as a state predicate: no
`Moved` leaf is readable. The other sentences concern `transfer` and are theorems. -/
def I4 (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ a p, s.I p = .moved → ¬ CanReadLeaf s a p

/-- `AnchorOrder` (B8 as corrected by C1): for every usable place and every anchor of it, the
frame of the effective anchor (`S3.effAnchor`, the root of the chain of origins) is the frame of
the place or one of its ancestors (MM-03.3.1, `ancestor`). It holds for every anchor. -/
def AnchorOrder (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)

/-- `I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4`, the invariant `Inv3` written in MM-03.3 §2, before the clause
`AnchorOrder` that B8 adds to it. -/
def Inv3base (s : S3) : Prop := I1 s ∧ I2 s ∧ I3 s ∧ I4 s

/-- `NoDangling` (C2): no active authority covers a leaf of a place that is not usable in the sense
of `Usable` (existence, `dead` mark, chain of owners). It says nothing of initialisation: a leaf
`Uninit` or `Moved` of a usable place may stay covered. -/
def NoDangling (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[j]? = some y → y.active = true →
    ∀ q, ¬ s.Usable q → ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, l ∉ y.footprint

/-- `Inv3` (MM-03.3 §2; B8, C1, C2): the safety invariant,
`I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4 ∧ AnchorOrder ∧ NoDangling`. -/
def Inv3 (s : S3) : Prop := Inv3base s ∧ AnchorOrder s ∧ NoDangling s

theorem Inv3.base {s : S3} (h : Inv3 s) : Inv3base s := h.1
theorem Inv3.ao {s : S3} (h : Inv3 s) : AnchorOrder s := h.2.1
theorem Inv3.nd {s : S3} (h : Inv3 s) : NoDangling s := h.2.2

/-- `AnchorOrder` read on the places of `P`: decidable form. -/
theorem anchorOrder_iff {s : S3} : AnchorOrder s ↔
    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q) :=
  ⟨fun h q _ hq => h q hq, fun h q hq => h q (List.mem_range.2 hq.lt) hq⟩

/-- `NoDangling` read on the authorities of `A` and on the places containing each covered leaf:
decidable form. -/
theorem noDangling_iff {s : S3} : NoDangling s ↔
    ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active j → ∀ l ∈ s.afp j, l < s.P.length → isLeaf s.P l →
      ∀ q ∈ l :: chain (parentOf s.P) l, s.Usable q := by
  constructor
  · intro h j _ ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ l hl hlP hleaf q hq
    have hl' : l ∈ y.footprint := by simpa [S3.afp, hy] using hl
    exact Decidable.byContradiction fun hu => h j y hy ya q hu l
      (mem_footprint.2 ⟨hlP, hleaf, hlP, (List.mem_cons.1 hq).imp Eq.symm id⟩) hl'
  · intro h j y hy ya q hu l hl hly
    obtain ⟨hlP, hleaf, -, hq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
    exact hu (h j (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy)) ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ l
      (by simp only [S3.afp, hy]; exact hly) hlP hleaf q (List.mem_cons.2 (hq.imp Eq.symm id)))

/-- I4 holds in every state: the read condition requires `Init` (MM-03.3 §2, I4; §5). -/
theorem i4_always (s : S3) : I4 s := fun _ _ hm h => by rw [h.2.1] at hm; cases hm

/-- Root place (MM-03.3.2; B1): an existing place without parent. -/
def RootPlace (P : List Place) (r : Nat) : Prop := r < P.length ∧ parentOf P r = none

instance (P : List Place) (r : Nat) : Decidable (RootPlace P r) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- First clause of B1: two distinct root places have disjoint footprints. Parts and their
containing places are not concerned. -/
def RootsDisjoint (P : List Place) : Prop :=
  ∀ r r', RootPlace P r → RootPlace P r' → r ≠ r' → ∀ l ∈ footprint P r, l ∉ footprint P r'

/-- Second clause of B1: the chain of origins of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root
authority of the root place of that leaf, an authority without origin whose footprint is the
footprint of that root place. -/
def RootChain (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority) (l : Nat), s.A[a]? = some y → l ∈ y.footprint → isLeaf s.P l →
    ∃ x z r, (x = a ∨ x ∈ s.ancs a) ∧ s.A[x]? = some z ∧ z.origin = none ∧ RootPlace s.P r ∧
      partOf s.P l r ∧ ∀ l', l' ∈ z.footprint ↔ l' ∈ footprint s.P r

/-- A4, "Une racine reste détenue par le propriétaire de son emplacement", a possession condition
that A1 keeps in `WF3`: an authority without origin is held by the owner of the root place of
every leaf it covers. -/
def RootHeld (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Nat) (z : Authority) (l r : Nat), s.A[x]? = some z → z.origin = none → l ∈ z.footprint →
    RootPlace s.P r → partOf s.P l r → ∃ pr, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner

/-- `WF3` (A1, A4, B1, C3): well-formedness, the domain of admissible states, separate from the
safety invariant `Inv3`. Origins precede their derivations; footprints are made of existing
places; the stack is non-empty and without duplicates, below `nF`; owner frames are below `nF`;
owner places exist; a part comes after its parent and has its owner and its `dead` flag; every
active authority has a live holder (possession); B1: the chain of origins of an authority covering
a leaf ends at the root authority of its root place (`RootChain`); A4: a root is held by the owner
of its place (`RootHeld`). C3: the first clause of B1, `RootsDisjoint`, is not a clause: it holds
for every list of places (`rootsDisjoint_always`). -/
def WF3 (s : S3) : Prop :=
  (∀ (b : Nat) (y : Authority) (a : Nat), s.A[b]? = some y → y.origin = some a → a < b) ∧
  (∀ (a : Nat) (x : Authority), s.A[a]? = some x → ∀ l ∈ x.footprint, l < s.P.length) ∧
  s.F ≠ [] ∧ s.F.Nodup ∧ (∀ f ∈ s.F, f < s.nF) ∧
  (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (f : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .frame f → f < s.nF) ∧
  (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (o : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o →
    o < s.P.length) ∧
  (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (r : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.parent = some r →
    ∃ pr : Place, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ r < q ∧ pr.owner = pl.owner ∧ s.dead r = s.dead q) ∧
  (∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[a]? = some y → y.active = true → HolderLive s y.holder) ∧
  RootChain s ∧ RootHeld s

/-- The pass-1 exclusivity on effective modes (MM-03.3 §2, I1) is a theorem under the
strengthened I1 (A1). -/
theorem effective_compat {s : S3} (h : I1 s) :
    ∀ a b p m₁ m₂, a ≠ b → effective s a p = some m₁ → effective s b p = some m₂ →
      Compat m₁ m₂ := by
  intro a b p m₁ m₂ hab ha hb
  obtain ⟨x, hx, xa, xp, ex⟩ := effective_some ha
  obtain ⟨y, hy, ya, yp, ey⟩ := effective_some hb
  have obs₁ : x.mode = .observe → m₁ = .observe := fun hm => by
    rcases effOf_cases ex with ⟨-, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, -, rfl⟩ <;> simp [hm]
  have obs₂ : y.mode = .observe → m₂ = .observe := fun hm => by
    rcases effOf_cases ey with ⟨-, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, -, rfl⟩ <;> simp [hm]
  by_cases hba : b ∈ s.ancs a
  · have hm : x.mode ∈ descModes s b p := mem_descModes.2 ⟨a, x, hx, xa, xp, hba, rfl⟩
    rcases effOf_cases ey with ⟨h0, -⟩ | ⟨-, hn, rfl⟩
    · simp [h0] at hm
    · have : x.mode = .observe := mode_eq_observe fun e => hn (e ▸ hm)
      exact ⟨obs₁ this, rfl⟩
  by_cases hab' : a ∈ s.ancs b
  · have hm : y.mode ∈ descModes s a p := mem_descModes.2 ⟨b, y, hy, ya, yp, hab', rfl⟩
    rcases effOf_cases ex with ⟨h0, -⟩ | ⟨-, hn, rfl⟩
    · simp [h0] at hm
    · have : y.mode = .observe := mode_eq_observe fun e => hn (e ▸ hm)
      exact ⟨rfl, obs₂ this⟩
  obtain ⟨h₁, h₂⟩ := h a b x y p hab hx hy xa ya xp yp hab' hba
  exact ⟨obs₁ h₁, obs₂ h₂⟩

/-- `effective_exclusive` (MM-03.3 §10): under I1, an authority with effective `Modify` on a leaf
is the only one with a present effective mode there. -/
theorem effective_exclusive {s : S3} (h : I1 s) {a b p : Nat} (hab : a ≠ b)
    (ha : effective s a p = some .modify) : effective s b p = none := by
  cases hb : effective s b p with
  | none => rfl
  | some m => exact absurd (effective_compat h a b p _ _ hab ha hb).1 (by simp)

/-- `shared_keeps_exclusivity` (A9): I1 holds on `SharedMutable` leaves like on any other leaf:
two unrelated active authorities covering such a leaf are both in `Observe`. -/
theorem shared_keeps_exclusivity {k : K} {s : S3} (h : I1 s) {a b : Nat} {x y : Authority}
    {p : Nat} (_hsh : k.SharedMutable p) (hab : a ≠ b) (hx : s.A[a]? = some x)
    (hy : s.A[b]? = some y) (xa : x.active = true) (ya : y.active = true)
    (xp : p ∈ x.footprint) (yp : p ∈ y.footprint) (hnab : a ∉ s.ancs b) (hnba : b ∉ s.ancs a) :
    x.mode = .observe ∧ y.mode = .observe :=
  h a b x y p hab hx hy xa ya xp yp hnab hnba

/-- Central theorem (MM-03.3 §5): in a state satisfying `Inv3base`, an authorised ordinary write
coexists with no other authority with a present effective mode on the written leaves. The proof
uses only the effective `Modify` of the writer. -/
theorem write3_exclusive {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} (hinv : Inv3base s)
    (h : Write3Step a ls s (.ok s')) : ∀ p ∈ ls, ∀ b, b ≠ a → effective s b p = none := by
  intro p hp b hb
  obtain ⟨⟨-, hw⟩, -⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  exact effective_exclusive hinv.1 (Ne.symm hb) (hw p hp).1

def I4 (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ a p, s.I p = .moved → ¬ CanReadLeaf s a p

/-- `AnchorOrder` (B8): every local anchor, without origin, of a usable place is held in a frame at
least as old as the frame of the place, that is, the frame of the place or one of its ancestors
(MM-03.3.1, `ancestor`). It is the non-escape restriction of MM-03.3.6 (`NoEscape`), which
constrains local anchors only (pass 1, (c) 13); a derived anchor is not constrained. See the
report, (c) 1, 2 and (e) 1. -/
def AnchorOrder (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, NoEscape s x (s.pframe q)

/-- `I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4`, the invariant `Inv3` written in MM-03.3 §2, before the clause
`AnchorOrder` that B8 adds to it. -/
def Inv3base (s : S3) : Prop := I1 s ∧ I2 s ∧ I3 s ∧ I4 s

/-- `Inv3` (MM-03.3 §2; B8): the safety invariant, `I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4 ∧ AnchorOrder`. -/
def Inv3 (s : S3) : Prop := Inv3base s ∧ AnchorOrder s

/-- `AnchorOrder` read on the places of `P`: decidable form. -/
theorem anchorOrder_iff {s : S3} : AnchorOrder s ↔
    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, NoEscape s x (s.pframe q) :=
  ⟨fun h q _ hq => h q hq, fun h q hq => h q (List.mem_range.2 hq.lt) hq⟩

/-- I4 holds in every state: the read condition requires `Init` (MM-03.3 §2, I4; §5). -/
theorem i4_always (s : S3) : I4 s := fun _ _ hm h => by rw [h.2.1] at hm; cases hm

/-- Root place (MM-03.3.2; B1): an existing place without parent. -/
def RootPlace (P : List Place) (r : Nat) : Prop := r < P.length ∧ parentOf P r = none

instance (P : List Place) (r : Nat) : Decidable (RootPlace P r) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- First clause of B1: two distinct root places have disjoint footprints. Parts and their
containing places are not concerned. -/
def RootsDisjoint (P : List Place) : Prop :=
  ∀ r r', RootPlace P r → RootPlace P r' → r ≠ r' → ∀ l ∈ footprint P r, l ∉ footprint P r'

/-- Second clause of B1: the chain of origins of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root
authority of the root place of that leaf, an authority without origin whose footprint is the
footprint of that root place. -/
def RootChain (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority) (l : Nat), s.A[a]? = some y → l ∈ y.footprint → isLeaf s.P l →
    ∃ x z r, (x = a ∨ x ∈ s.ancs a) ∧ s.A[x]? = some z ∧ z.origin = none ∧ RootPlace s.P r ∧
      partOf s.P l r ∧ ∀ l', l' ∈ z.footprint ↔ l' ∈ footprint s.P r

/-- A4, "Une racine reste détenue par le propriétaire de son emplacement", a possession condition
that A1 keeps in `WF3`: an authority without origin is held by the owner of the root place of
every leaf it covers. -/
def RootHeld (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ (x : Nat) (z : Authority) (l r : Nat), s.A[x]? = some z → z.origin = none → l ∈ z.footprint →
    RootPlace s.P r → partOf s.P l r → ∃ pr, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner

/-- `WF3` (A1, A4, B1): well-formedness, the domain of admissible states, separate from the safety
invariant `Inv3`. Origins precede their derivations; footprints are made of existing places;
the stack is non-empty and without duplicates, below `nF`; owner frames are below `nF`; owner
places exist; a part comes after its parent and has its owner and its `dead` flag; every active
authority has a live holder (possession); B1: distinct root places have disjoint footprints
(`RootsDisjoint`, a property of every list of places, `rootsDisjoint_always`); the chain of
origins of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root authority of its root place
(`RootChain`); A4: a root is held by the owner of its place (`RootHeld`). -/
def WF3 (s : S3) : Prop :=
  (∀ (b : Nat) (y : Authority) (a : Nat), s.A[b]? = some y → y.origin = some a → a < b) ∧
  (∀ (a : Nat) (x : Authority), s.A[a]? = some x → ∀ l ∈ x.footprint, l < s.P.length) ∧
  s.F ≠ [] ∧ s.F.Nodup ∧ (∀ f ∈ s.F, f < s.nF) ∧
  (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (f : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .frame f → f < s.nF) ∧
  (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (o : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o →
    o < s.P.length) ∧
  (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (r : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.parent = some r →
    ∃ pr : Place, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ r < q ∧ pr.owner = pl.owner ∧ s.dead r = s.dead q) ∧
  (∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[a]? = some y → y.active = true → HolderLive s y.holder) ∧
  RootsDisjoint s.P ∧ RootChain s ∧ RootHeld s

strengthened I1 (A1). -/
theorem effective_compat {s : S3} (h : I1 s) :
    ∀ a b p m₁ m₂, a ≠ b → effective s a p = some m₁ → effective s b p = some m₂ →
      Compat m₁ m₂ := by

  obtain ⟨y, hy, ya, yp, ey⟩ := effective_some hb

    rcases effOf_cases ex with ⟨-, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, -, rfl⟩ <;> simp [hm]
  have obs₂ : y.mode = .observe → m₂ = .observe := fun hm => by
    rcases effOf_cases ey with ⟨-, rfl⟩ | ⟨-, -, rfl⟩ <;> simp [hm]

  · have hm : x.mode ∈ descModes s b p := mem_descModes.2 ⟨a, x, hx, xa, xp, hba, rfl⟩
    rcases effOf_cases ey with ⟨h0, -⟩ | ⟨-, hn, rfl⟩
    · simp [h0] at hm
    · have : x.mode = .observe := mode_eq_observe fun e => hn (e ▸ hm)
      exact ⟨obs₁ this, rfl⟩

  · have hm : y.mode ∈ descModes s a p := mem_descModes.2 ⟨b, y, hy, ya, yp, hab', rfl⟩
    rcases effOf_cases ex with ⟨h0, -⟩ | ⟨-, hn, rfl⟩
    · simp [h0] at hm

      exact ⟨rfl, obs₂ this⟩

  exact ⟨obs₁ h₁, obs₂ h₂⟩

/-- `effective_exclusive` (MM-03.3 §10): under I1, an authority with effective `Modify` on a leaf
is the only one with a present effective mode there. -/
theorem effective_exclusive {s : S3} (h : I1 s) {a b p : Nat} (hab : a ≠ b)
    (ha : effective s a p = some .modify) : effective s b p = none := by
  cases hb : effective s b p with
  | none => rfl
  | some m => exact absurd (effective_compat h a b p _ _ hab ha hb).1 (by simp)

1. **`Inv3` complet est un invariant des états atteints.** `Inv3 := Inv3base ∧ AnchorOrder ∧ NoDangling` (C1, C2). `reachable_access_invariant_underDD` conclut `WF3 s ∧ Inv3 s`, sous `DDSound k`. content.content:
`Inv3base` reste le nom de `I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4` : les énoncés de la passe 3 qui en parlent gardent leur texte.

Décisions de la passe 4 :

1. **Ancre effective (C1).** « la racine de sa chaîne d'origines (`RootChain`) » : `S3.effAnchor s x` est le dernier élément de `x :: ancs x`, la chaîne suivie par `RootChain` et le ré-ancrage de A7. Sous l'ordre des origines de `WF3`, elle n'a pas d'origine (`effAnchor_root`). Pour une ancre sans origine, c'est l'ancre elle-même.
2. **`EffAnchorOK` sans cas permissif.** `EffAnchorOK s x fd` exige que l'ancre effective existe, que son détenteur ait un cadre, que le dépendant en ait un, et que le premier soit le second ou un de ses ancêtres. `NoEscape` (passe 3) admettait par défaut une ancre sans cadre ou un emplacement sans cadre. L'activité de l'ancre effective n'est pas exigée : C1 n'en parle pas, et I3 porte sur l'ancre elle-même.
3. **Clause B8 de `transfer` (C1).** Elle contrôle l'ancre effective quand celle-ci bouge avec la valeur, comme en passe 3, et aussi quand le dépendant bouge : la destination, ou un emplacement que la valeur possède. Sans ce second cas, le `transfer` du cas 10 serait accepté et violerait `AnchorOrder` dans l'état d'arrivée : C1 (« Vaut pour toutes les ancres ») et l'étape 1 (`WF3 ∧ Inv3` sur les états atteints) l'excluent. C'est aussi MM-03.3.6 lu sur l'ancre effective : « Une valeur dépendante ne peut être installée dans une destination dont le cadre survivrait à celui d'une ancre locale dont elle dépend ». La clause découle de `AnchorOrder` de l'état d'arrivée : elle ne rejette que les transferts qui le violeraient. Conséquence : les cas 10 et n9 sont rejetés au `transfer` ((g)).
4. **`NoEscape` gardé dans `DependPre` et dans la clause 6 de `TransferPre` (B7).** C1 ne retire pas ces clauses. Pour une ancre sans origine, l'ancre effective est l'ancre elle-même, et `EffAnchorOK` au même cadre implique `NoEscape` ; pour une ancre dérivée, `NoEscape` ne dit rien.
5. **`NoDangling` (C2), lu à la lettre.** Pour toute autorité active, tout emplacement non utilisable et toute feuille de son empreinte, l'autorité ne couvre pas cette feuille. L'initialisation n'est pas lue.
6. **Hypothèses des préservations.** Chaque préservation d'`AnchorOrder` prend `AnchorOrder s`, et `WF3 s` quand elle en a besoin. Chaque préservation de `NoDangling` prend `NoDangling s`, plus `WF3 s` et `Inv3base s` pour `endUse` et `free`. `reachable_access_invariant_underDD` les assemble.
7. **`RootsDisjoint` (C3).** Sorti de `WF3`, gardé comme définition et théorème (`rootsDisjoint_always`). Les exemples qui énumèrent les clauses de `WF3` pour `xferCex` et `nd0` le gardent, comme en passe 3.
8. **`release` (C4).** Dernière clause de `ReleasePre` : l'autorité a une origine, et son détenteur est le cadre courant ou un emplacement `p` avec `HasRight s .modify p`. `HasRight` est le droit `Modify` exerçable de B2, déjà demandé par `transfer`, `endUse` et `free`. La disjonction de la passe 3 (« exerçable à un mode ») disparaît.
9. **`endUse` (C5, C8).** Dernière clause de `EndUsePre` : aucune feuille finissante épinglée, statiquement ou dynamiquement, quel que soit `ExternalDone`. `endUseS` marque mortes les places possédées par `p` ou une de ses parties, jamais `p` : déjà conforme à C8, aucune correction. Cas de la passe 4 : un local fini puis réécrit et relu.
10. **`StaticPinnedBottom` (C5).** « toute feuille couverte par `K.Pinned` appartient à un emplacement possédé, transitivement, par le cadre de base » : `∀ l, K.Pinned l → ∃ q, l ∈ footprint s.P q ∧ OwnedByFrame s.P (s.F.getLastD 0) q`. Le cadre de base est le dernier de la pile, que la sortie ne retire jamais. Sous `WF3`, tous les emplacements qui contiennent une feuille ont le même propriétaire : la forme existentielle équivaut à la forme universelle. Hypothèse nommée du seul `static_pinned_never_exits`.
11. **`static_pinned_never_exits`.** Pour un état `WF3` de pile `f :: F₀` avec `F₀ ≠ []`, sous `StaticPinnedBottom` : un emplacement utilisable avant la sortie et plus après ne couvre aucune feuille de `K.Pinned`. C'est la partie statique de la clause B4 de `ExitPre`.
12. **Forme de `alloc` (C6).** `List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)`, comme les locaux de `enterFrame` : parent, élément propriétaire, `kind`, en indices absolus.
    - `ShapeOK n ls` est mot pour mot la troisième clause de `EnterPre` (`enterPre_shapeOK`). `EnterPre` est inchangé.
    - `allocP s owner ls := shapeP s.P (.place owner) ls`, et `enterP s ls = shapeP s.P (.frame s.nF) ls` (`enterP_eq_shapeP`, par `rfl`).
    - La composante « élément propriétaire » garde son sens de `enterFrame` : un élément peut être possédé par un élément antérieur ; les autres sont possédés par `owner`.
    - Une racine d'autorité `Modify` par élément racine, sur son empreinte, détenue par le propriétaire de l'élément (A4).
13. **Métadonnées du fournisseur (C6).** Ce sont les feuilles du fournisseur, celles sur lesquelles `ProviderRight` (B5) donne le droit de mise à jour. `AllocStatic` exige qu'elles soient toutes `Init` ; l'effet les met à `Init`, comme `issue` pour l'arène. Sous la précondition, cette écriture ne change pas `I`.
14. **`Satisfiable` (C9).** `K.Satisfiable provider shape s`, lu dans l'état avant `alloc`. Ordre des issues inchangé : `reject` si une précondition statique échoue, sinon `fail` si `Satisfiable` est faux, sinon `ok`. Aucun théorème ne le suppose vrai.
15. **`MetaRight` (C6).** Premier disjoint ajouté : `Modify` exerçable sur la valeur arène (`OptP (arenaValue s ar) (HasRight s .modify) False`). `ResetPre` lit le même `MetaRight` depuis la passe 2 : l'alignement vaut aussi pour `reset`.
16. **Théorèmes de la passe 3 sur `alloc`.** `alloc_fresh` est généralisé à tous les indices nouveaux. `alloc_owned_root` est énoncé par élément racine ; sa clause « l'empreinte est l'emplacement lui-même », propre à une feuille, passe dans `alloc_owned_root_leaf`, qui reprend mot pour mot les conjoints de la passe 3 pour la forme `[(none, none, 0)]`.
17. **Forme vide.** `ShapeOK n []` vaut et aucune précondition ne l'exclut : `alloc` de `[]` est `ok`, sans emplacement ni autorité. Question (e) 2.
18. **Témoins sans `WF3`.** `transfer_not_inv3_preserving` garde son énoncé de la passe 3 sur un nouveau `xferCex`, qui satisfait l'`Inv3` complet : la source a un lien de parent vers un emplacement d'indice supérieur, que `chain` ignore, si bien qu'elle ne couvre aucune feuille. L'ancien témoin, `xferNd`, viole `NoDangling` : il reste en `example`. Le témoin de `alloc_not_inv3_preserving` a ses feuilles `Init`, comme C6 l'exige du fournisseur.

## (d) Théorèmes non prouvés tels que demandés, et pourquoi

1. **`static_pinned_never_exits`** est prouvé, sous `WF3` et `StaticPinnedBottom`. Sur un état atteint, l'hypothèse force `K.Pinned` vide (`staticPinnedBottom_forces_empty`), et la conclusion est alors triviale. Question (e) 1.
2. **Inchangés depuis la passe 3** : passe 2, (d) 2 (`DDSound` nécessaire), 3 (`Reachable` sans `issue` ni `reset`) et 6 (pas de totalité).
3. **Théorèmes qui réénoncent une précondition** (passe 2, (d) 5 ; passe 3, (d) 4). Inchangés ; `alloc_fail_unchanged` lit maintenant `Satisfiable pr ls s`.

La passe 3, (d) 1 (`AnchorOrder` non préservé par la sortie) est résolue par C1. La passe 3, (d) 2 vaut toujours, avec des témoins qui satisfont l'`Inv3` complet.

Questions de la passe 3, toutes tranchées : 1 et 2 (C1), 3 (C3), 4 (C2), 5 et 9 (C5), 6 (C6), 7 (C7), 8 (C4). Questions de la passe 2 encore ouvertes : 13 (`WF3` dans la spécification). 1. **`StaticPinnedBottom` sur les états atteints** ((c) 10, (d) 1). L'état initial a un cadre et aucun emplacement (brief de la passe 1 : « un cadre, aucun emplacement »). `enterFrame` donne à ses locaux le nouveau cadre ou un emplacement pour propriétaire, `alloc` et `transfer` un emplacement. ## (i) Énoncés de la passe 3 retirés ou réécrits

Comparaison mécanique des énoncés (hypothèses et conclusion jusqu'au `:=` de niveau zéro) entre `31d90e3` et `90ac654` :
- 369 théorèmes en passe 3, 421 en passe 4 ;
- 327 au texte inchangé ;
- 31 réécrits ;
- 11 retirés, remplacés.

### Énoncés retirés (11)

| Passe 3 | Remplacé par | Raison |
|---|---|---|
| `allocP_new`, `allocP_get`, `alloc_parentOf_new`, `alloc_parentOf_lt`, `alloc_footprint_new_sub`, `alloc_footprint_old` | `shapeP_new`, `shapeP_get`, `shape_parentOf_new`, `shape_parentOf_lt`, `shape_root_fp_ge`, `shape_footprint_old` | C6 : l'emplacement créé n'est plus une feuille unique d'indice `|P|` ; les lemmes portent sur une forme. |

### Énoncés réécrits (31)

**C1 (3).**
- `anchorOrder_iff` : forme décidable de la nouvelle définition.
- `AnchorOrder.of` : l'hypothèse `I3 s` disparaît ; une hypothèse `hanc` (chaînes d'origines inchangées sur les autorités existantes) s'ajoute. `AnchorOrder` lit maintenant l'ancre effective, qui dépend des chaînes. Toutes les opérations la satisfont (les origines ne changent que par la sortie, traitée à part).
- `AnchorOrder.frames` : hypothèses `WF3` et `I3` renommées `_hwf`, `_h3`, devenues inutiles ; énoncé gardé.

**Préservations d'`AnchorOrder` (13).** `Inv3 s` → `AnchorOrder s` : renforcement. `Inv3` contient maintenant `NoDangling`, que ces preuves n'utilisent pas. Énoncés : `derive_`, `split_`, `release_`, `depend_`, `write3_`, `pinEff_`, `endUse_`, `free_`, `enter_`, `alloc_`, `transfer_`, `issue_`, `reset_preserves_anchorOrder`. Pour `alloc_preserves_anchorOrder`, aussi la signature de C6.

**`reachable_access_invariant_underDD` (1).** `WF3 ∧ Inv3base` → `WF3 ∧ Inv3` : renforcement demandé par l'étape 1.

**`alloc` (13).** Signature de C6 et C9 : fournisseur et forme en paramètres de `allocEff`, `Satisfiable` lu sur la forme et l'état.
- Contenu inchangé : `alloc_det`, `alloc_fail_unchanged`, `allocP_lt`, `alloc_usable_old`, `alloc_usable_back`, `alloc_ancs_lt`, `alloc_rootHeld`, `alloc_preserves`, `alloc_frameOf_old`, `alloc_pframe_old`.

- `alloc_fresh` : généralisé à tous les indices `|P| + i` et `|A| + j` ; pour `i = j = 0` et la forme d'une feuille, c'est l'énoncé de la passe 3.
- `alloc_owned_root` : énoncé par élément racine, sans l'hypothèse `WF3`. Le conjoint « l'empreinte est l'emplacement lui-même », propre à une feuille, est dans `alloc_owned_root_leaf`, qui reprend mot pour mot les cinq conjoints de la passe 3 pour la forme `[(none, none, 0)]`.

**`alloc_not_inv3_preserving` (1).** État témoin `Init` (C6 exige un fournisseur `Init`), forme `[(none, none, 0)]`. La conclusion est la même.

**Sens nouveau des définitions, à texte inchangé.**
- `Inv3` reçoit `NoDangling` (C2). `enter_not_inv3_preserving`, `transfer_not_inv3_preserving` et `exitFrame_no_dangling_needs_rootHeld` concluent `Inv3` de leur témoin : leur sens se renforce. Aucun énoncé gardé ne suppose `Inv3`.

- `MetaRight` (C6) est plus large. Les théorèmes qui supposent un `issue` ou un `reset` acceptés portent sur plus de pas ; leurs preuves valent telles quelles.

Hormis `hanc` dans `AnchorOrder.of` (lemme technique, justifié ci-dessus), aucune hypothèse n'est ajoutée à un énoncé de la passe 3.

/-- Preconditions of `exitFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, O7; A7; B4): the exiting frame has a caller; every
anchor of a place still usable after the exit has a surviving authority among itself and its
ancestors along `origin`; every surviving derived authority has a surviving strict ancestor;
B4: no leaf of a place that dies with the frame, transitively owned storage included, is
pinned, dynamically (A8) or statically (`Pinned`, MM-03.3.8). Otherwise the exit is rejected. -/
def ExitPre (k : K) (s : S3) : Prop :=
  match s.F with
  | _ :: F₀ => F₀ ≠ [] ∧
      (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, ({ s with F := F₀ } : S3).Usable q →
        ∀ x ∈ s.D q, firstSurv s F₀ (x :: s.ancs x) ≠ none) ∧
      (∀ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, Survives s F₀ a → s.org a ≠ none →
        firstSurv s F₀ (s.ancs a) ≠ none) ∧
      (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ¬ ({ s with F := F₀ } : S3).Usable q →
        ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l)
  | [] => False

instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) : Decidable (ExitPre k s) := by
  unfold ExitPre; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Effect of `exitFrame` (MM-03.3 §4, O7; A4; A5; A7): return to the caller; each anchor
replaced by the first surviving authority among itself and its ancestors; authorities that do
not survive released; surviving derived authorities re-attached. -/
def exitEff (s : S3) : S3 :=
  match s.F with
  | _ :: F₀ =>
    { s with
      F := F₀
      D := fun q => (s.D q).map fun x => (firstSurv s F₀ (x :: s.ancs x)).getD x
      A := mapI (exitG s F₀) 0 s.A }
  | [] => s

/-- `exitFrame` as a relation (MM-03.3 §4, O7). -/
def ExitStep (k : K) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop := Guarded (ExitPre k s) (exitEff s)

/-! ## Abstract reads and writes (MM-03.3 §5) -/

/-- Ordinary read condition of a leaf by authority `a` (MM-03.3 §5, `canRead3`): an effective
authority permits observation, the leaf is initialised, the needed dependencies are valid. The
type and storage contract is not represented. -/
def CanReadLeaf (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Prop :=
  effective s a p ≠ none ∧ s.I p = .init ∧ DepsValid s p

instance (s : S3) (a p : Nat) : Decidable (CanReadLeaf s a p) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- `canRead3` (MM-03.3 §5): ordinary read of leaves `ls` by authority `a`, exercisable at
`Observe` (B2). -/
def canRead3 (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Prop :=
    | place hpl _ ho' _ =>
      have : (exitEff s).P = s.P := by rw [e]
      rw [this, hq] at hpl; cases hpl; rw [ho] at ho'; cases ho'

/-- Place `q` belongs to frame `f` through ownership (A5): it is owned by `f`, or by a place that
belongs to `f`. -/
inductive OwnedByFrame (P : List Place) (f : Nat) : Nat → Prop where
  | frame {q : Nat} {pl : Place} : P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .frame f → OwnedByFrame P f q
  | place {q o : Nat} {pl : Place} : P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o → OwnedByFrame P f o →
      OwnedByFrame P f q

/-- After the exit, no place that belongs to the exited frame through ownership is usable
(MM-03.3.1; MM-03.3 §4, O7; A5): the locals of the frame and their owned storage, transitively. -/
theorem exitFrame_kills_owned {k : K} {s s' : S3} {f : Nat} {F₀ : Frames} (hwf : WF3 s) (hinv : Inv3base s)
    (hF : s.F = f :: F₀) (h : ExitStep k s (.ok s')) :
    ∀ q, OwnedByFrame s.P f q → ¬ s'.Usable q := by
  have hk := (exitFrame_kills_locals hwf hinv hF h).2.1
  have hP : s'.P = s.P := by obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h; rw [exitEff_eq hF]
  intro q hq
  induction hq with
  | @frame q pl hpl ho => exact hk q pl hpl ho
    exact exitFrame_no_dangling hwf hF h q (exit_owned_of_usable hF hq₀ hq₁) j _ hz za l hl hlz
  · rw [(exitG_same s F₀ j y₀).2.1] at hlz
    exact hnd j y₀ hy₀ (exitG_active' hy₀ za) q hq₀ l hl hlz

/-- `StaticPinnedBottom k s` (C5), obligation on the static pinning `K.Pinned`: every leaf covered
by `K.Pinned` belongs to a place owned, transitively, by the base frame, the last of the stack.
Dynamic pinning (`pin`, `unpin`) is not concerned. -/
def StaticPinnedBottom (k : K) (s : S3) : Prop :=
  ∀ l, k.Pinned l → ∃ q, l ∈ footprint s.P q ∧ OwnedByFrame s.P (s.F.getLastD 0) q

/-- A place has at most one owning frame (A5). -/
theorem OwnedByFrame.unique {P : List Place} {f g q : Nat} (h : OwnedByFrame P f q)
    (h' : OwnedByFrame P g q) : f = g := by
  induction h with
  | @frame q pl hpl ho =>
    cases h' with
    | frame hpl' ho' => rw [hpl] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [ho] at ho'; cases ho'; rfl
    | place hpl' ho' _ => rw [hpl] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [ho] at ho'; cases ho'
  | @place q o pl hpl ho _ ih =>
    cases h' with
    | frame hpl' ho' => rw [hpl] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [ho] at ho'; cases ho'
    | place hpl' ho' h'' => rw [hpl] at hpl'; cases hpl'; rw [ho] at ho'; cases ho'; exact ih h''

/-- `static_pinned_never_exits` (C5): under `StaticPinnedBottom`, no frame exit meets a statically
pinned leaf: a place that stops being usable at the exit covers no leaf of `K.Pinned`. -/
theorem static_pinned_never_exits {k : K} {s : S3} {f : Nat} {F₀ : Frames} (hwf : WF3 s)
    (hsp : StaticPinnedBottom k s) (hF : s.F = f :: F₀) (hne : F₀ ≠ []) :
    ∀ q, s.Usable q → ¬ ({ s with F := F₀ } : S3).Usable q →
      ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, ¬ k.Pinned l := by
  intro q hq hq' l hl hpin
  have hof := exit_owned_of_usable hF hq hq'
  obtain ⟨q', hl', hob⟩ := hsp l hpin
  obtain ⟨-, -, hlq⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl
  obtain ⟨-, -, hlq'⟩ := mem_footprint.1 hl'
  obtain ⟨pl, pq, hpl, hpq, e⟩ := hwf.ownerOf hlq
  obtain ⟨pl', pq', hpl', hpq', e'⟩ := hwf.ownerOf hlq'
  rw [hpl] at hpl'; cases hpl'
  have hfb := (hof.of_owner hpq hpl e).unique (hob.of_owner hpq' hpl e')
  obtain ⟨g, F₁, rfl⟩ : ∃ g F₁, F₀ = g :: F₁ := by
    cases F₀ with
    | nil => exact absurd rfl hne
    | cons g F₁ => exact ⟨g, F₁, rfl⟩
  rw [hF, List.getLastD_cons, List.getLastD_cons] at hfb
  have hnd := (List.nodup_cons.1 (hF ▸ hwf.nodup)).1
  exact hnd (by rw [hfb]; exact List.getLastD_mem_cons)

/-- An active authority after `endUse p` (A6): active before, not held within `p`, with a holder
live after `endUseS`. -/
theorem endUse_active {s : S3} {p j : Nat} {z : Authority}
    (hz : (endUseEff s p).A[j]? = some z) (za : z.active = true) :
    s.A[j]? = some z ∧ ¬ heldIn s.P p z.holder ∧ HolderLive (endUseS s p) z.holder := by

14:A5. `Place.owner : Frame | Place` (stockage possédé). `Usable` : la chaîne des propriétaires aboutit à un cadre sur la pile. Le transfert d'une valeur transfère la possession de ses emplacements possédés sans les déplacer. Un emplacement possédé n'est pas nécessairement une allocation distincte de MM-02 ; la correspondance relève du jalon 2.
21:A8. Épinglage dynamique : `pin p`/`unpin p` dans l'état. `transfer` rejeté si la source a une feuille en place épinglée ; les emplacements possédés épinglés n'empêchent pas le transfert (ils ne bougent pas). `free` et `endUse` rejetés sur une feuille épinglée sans `K.ExternalDone`. `unpin` exige `K.ExternalDone p`. `K.Pinned` reste pour l'épinglage statique.
27:1. A4, A5 : `holder`, `owner`, `Usable` réécrit, `transfer` sans `auths`, `exitFrame` sur la possession transitive.
20:4. **Préservation** : `Inv3` préservé par chaque opération sur `ok` ; `reachable_access_invariant` depuis un état initial (un cadre, aucun emplacement). Théorèmes du §10, plus `effective_exclusive`, `exitFrame_releases_all`, `dependent_cannot_escape_frame`, `exitFrame_reanchors_to_origin`, et le théorème central du §5.

/-- `endUse` preserves `NoDangling` (C2; A6), under `WF3`: an active authority on a leaf of a place
that stops being usable is derived, and released by `EndUseAccessOK`, or a root, held by the owner
of its root place (`RootChain`, `RootHeld`), which stops being usable too. -/
theorem endUse_preserves_noDangling {k : K} {s s' : S3} {p : Nat} (hwf : WF3 s)
    (hinv : Inv3base s) (hnd : NoDangling s) (h : EndUseStep k p s (.ok s')) : NoDangling s' := by
  have hw' := (endUse_preserves hwf hinv h).1
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  have hU : ∀ r, (endUseEff s p).Usable r ↔ (endUseS s p).Usable r :=

    · simp only [hc, ↓reduceIte] at hz
      split at hz
      · rename_i hl; subst hz; exact ⟨rfl, hc, hl⟩
      · subst hz; simp at za

/-- `free` preserves `NoDangling` (C2; A6), under `WF3`: the leaves of `p` are covered by no active
authority (`free_no_dangling`); on a leaf of another place that stops being usable, an active
authority is derived, and released by `FreeAccessOK`, or a root, held by the owner of its root
place (`RootChain`, `RootHeld`), which stops being usable too. -/
theorem free_preserves_noDangling {k : K} {s s' : S3} {p auth : Nat} (hwf : WF3 s)
    (hinv : Inv3base s) (hnd : NoDangling s) (h : FreeStep k p auth s (.ok s')) : NoDangling s' := by
  have hw' := (free_preserves hwf hinv h).1
  have hfd := free_no_dangling hwf hinv h
  obtain ⟨hpre, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 h
  have hU : ∀ r, (freeEff s p).Usable r ↔ (freeS s p).Usable r :=
    fun r => S3.Usable.congr (s := freeS s p) (s' := freeEff s p) rfl rfl rfl

    obtain ⟨pr, hpr, hh⟩ := hwf.rootHeld j z l r hz₀ hzo hlz hr hlr
    have hrp : ¬ partOf s.P r p := fun hrp => by
      obtain ⟨-, e | hc⟩ := hrp
      · subst e; exact hlp (mem_footprint.2 ⟨(mem_footprint.1 hl).1, hleaf, hlr⟩)
      · rw [chain_none hr.2] at hc; simp at hc
    have hd : (freeS s p).dead r = false := by
      simp only [freeS, (hwf.deadOf hlr).symm, hl₀.dead_false, Bool.false_or,
        decide_eq_false_iff_not]
      exact hrp
    have hr₁ : (freeS s p).Usable r := S3.Usable.of_owner hpr hd (hh ▸ hlive)

`Inv3`. Conditional on the obligation `DDSound k` of `DeclaredDisjoint` (MM-03.3.8), used by
`split`. -/
theorem reachable_access_invariant_underDD {k : K} (hdd : DDSound k) {s : S3}
    (h : Reachable k s) : WF3 s ∧ Inv3 s := by
  have mk : ∀ {s : S3}, WF3 s ∧ Inv3base s → AnchorOrder s → NoDangling s → WF3 s ∧ Inv3 s :=
    fun h a d => ⟨h.1, h.2, a, d⟩

        effective (enterEff s [] [(none, none, 0)]) b p = some m₂ → Compat m₁ m₂ := by

/-- Strict ancestors of `i` along the link `org`, nearest first. -/
def chainF (org : Nat → Option Nat) : Nat → Nat → List Nat
  | 0, _ => []
  | k + 1, i =>
    match org i with
    | some o => if o < i then o :: chainF org k o else []
    | none => []

/-- Strict ancestors of `i` along `org` (fuel `i`, enough since the chain decreases). -/
def chain (org : Nat → Option Nat) (i : Nat) : List Nat := chainF org i i

theorem chainF_none {org : Nat → Option Nat} {i : Nat} (h : org i = none) :
    ∀ k, chainF org k i = []
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))

/-- Storage leaf (MM-03.3.2): a place without a strict part. -/
def isLeaf (P : List Place) (l : Nat) : Prop := ∀ r < P.length, parentOf P r ≠ some l

instance (P : List Place) (l : Nat) : Decidable (isLeaf P l) :=
  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ _, _))

/-- `footprint P q` (MM-03.3.2): the leaves of `P` that are parts of `q`. -/
def footprint (P : List Place) (q : Nat) : List Nat :=
  (List.range P.length).filter fun l => decide (isLeaf P l ∧ partOf P l q)

/-- Two places overlap when their footprints share a leaf (MM-03.3.2). -/
def overlap (P : List Place) (p q : Nat) : Prop := ∃ l ∈ footprint P p, l ∈ footprint P q
